name: Mixture of hidden Markov trees

title: \bf Remark
body_md:
For fixed component topologies, a distribution in the class $\mathcal{M}_{J,R}$ has $O\big(RLJ(J+V)\big)$ parameters.
This representation complexity can be much smaller than the support size: even a single component with strictly positive emission kernel has full support on $\mathbb V^L$.
Consequently, guarantees that scale with the support size may incur a dependence on $V^L$, even when the distribution admits a compact representation with small $J$ and $R$.
 
Mixtures enrich this representation by allowing components to differ in tree topology, transitions, and emissions \citep{meila2000mixtures}, while increasing the parameter count only linearly in $R$.
To illustrate this, suppose that all components share a common tree topology.
The mixture can then be represented as a single HMT with $RJ$ states with block diagonal transition matrices.
This structure requires only $O(LRJ^2)$ transition parameters, reduced from $O(LR^2J^2)$ for a generic $RJ$-state HMT with dense transitions.

label: lem:continuous latent representation
title: \bf Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We approximate the latent variable by a finite grid. Let $s=\lfloor R^{1/k}\rfloor\geq1$, and partition $[0,1]^k$ into $s^k\leq R$ cubes $\{C_j\}_{j=1}^{s^k}$ of side length $1/s$, assigning their boundaries so that the cells are disjoint. Denote by $z_j$ the midpoint of $C_j$, and define
\[
    w_j:=\mu(C_j),\qquad
    q_R(x):=\sum_{j=1}^{s^k}w_j\prod_{i=1}^L p_i(x_i\mid z_j).
\]
Since each component is a product distribution, $q_R\in\mathcal M_{1,R}$. For $z\in[0,1]^k$, let $j(z)$ be the index of its cell. Consider the joint distributions
\[
    P(\mathrm{d} z,x):=\mu(\mathrm{d} z)\prod_{i=1}^L p_i(x_i\mid z),
    \qquad
    Q(\mathrm{d} z,x):=\mu(\mathrm{d} z)\prod_{i=1}^L p_i(x_i\mid z_{j(z)}).
\]
Their marginals on $x$ are $p^\star$ and $q_R$, respectively:
\begin{align*}
    \int_{[0,1]^k} Q(\mathrm{d} z,x) = \int_{[0,1]^k} \prod_{i=1}^L p_i(x_i\mid z_{j(z)})\,\mu(\mathrm{d} z) = \sum_{j=1}^{s^k} \int_{C_j} \prod_{i=1}^L p_i(x_i\mid z_{j})\,\mu(\mathrm{d} z) = q_R(x).
\end{align*}
By the data-processing inequality and the chain rule for KL divergence,
\begin{align*}
    D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p^\star\, \| \, q_R)
    &\leq D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\, \|\, Q)\\
    &=\int_{[0,1]^k}\sum_{i=1}^L
      D_{\mathrm{KL}}\big(p_i(\cdot\mid z)\,\|\,p_i(\cdot\mid z_{j(z)})\big)\,\mu(\mathrm{d} z)\\
    &\leq LA^2\int_{[0,1]^k}\|z-z_{j(z)}\|_2^{2\alpha}\,\mu(\mathrm{d} z)\\
    &\leq LA^2\bigg(\frac{\sqrt{k}}{2s}\bigg)^{2\alpha}
     \leq k^\alpha LA^2R^{-2\alpha/k}.
\end{align*}
Here the last two inequalities control the maximum distance to the cell midpoint and $s\geq R^{1/k}/2$. Together with $\mathcal M_{1,R}\subseteq\mathcal M_{J,R}$, this proves \eqref{eq:cont latent repre proj error} with $C_{k,\alpha}=k^\alpha$.

It remains to verify the sufficient condition \eqref{eq:continuous latent repre sufficient for KL}. Let $F(a):=\log\sum_{v=1}^V e^{a_v}$. For $u=\operatorname{softmax}(a)$, we have
\[
    \nabla F(a)=u,\qquad
    \nabla^2F(a)=\operatorname{diag}(u)-uu^\top,
    \qquad \|\nabla^2F(a)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq1.
\]
For any $a,b\in\mathbb R^V$,
\begin{align*}
    D_{\mathrm{KL}}\big(\mathrm{softmax}(a)\,\|\,\operatorname{softmax}(b)\big)
    &= \sum_{v=1}^V \big(\mathrm{softmax}(a)_v\log\mathrm{softmax}(a)_v - \mathrm{softmax}(a)_v\log\mathrm{softmax}(b)_v\big)\\
    &=F(b)-F(a)-\nabla F(a)^\top(b-a)\\
    &\leq\frac12\|b-a\|_2^2.
\end{align*}
Taking $a=g_i(z)$ and $b=g_i(z')$, and applying \eqref{eq:continuous latent repre sufficient for KL} gives
\[
    D_{\mathrm{KL}}\big(p_i(\cdot\mid z)\,\|\,p_i(\cdot\mid z')\big)
    \leq\frac12\|g_i(z)-g_i(z')\|_2^2
    \leq A^2\|z-z'\|_2^{2\alpha}.
\]
This implies \eqref{eq:continuour latent repre KL condition} and completes the proof.

name: Lemma \reflem:continuous latent representation

label: lem:renyi-compression
title: \bf Lemma
head: environment
name: Approximation under low R\'enyi entropy

title: Proof
body_md:
We maintain the $R-1$ largest atoms and approximate the remaining mass by a uniform distribution. Enumerate the points of $\mathbb V^L$ as $x_{(1)},\ldots,x_{(V^L)}$, with probabilities $p_{(j)}:=p^\star(x_{(j)})$ in decreasing order. Set $p_{(j)}=0$ for $j>V^L$, and let
\[
    S_\alpha:=\sum_{j\geq1}p_{(j)}^\alpha
    =e^{(1-\alpha)H_\alpha(p^\star)},\quad
    \tau_{R-1}:=\sum_{j\geq R}p_{(j)}.
\]
If $\tau_{R-1}=0$, then $p^\star$ is a mixture of at most $R-1$ point masses. Each point mass is a product distribution, so $\mathsf{Proj}_{1,R}(p^\star)=0$.

For $\tau_{R-1}>0$, let $u$ be the uniform distribution on $\mathbb V^L$, and define
\[
    q_R:=\sum_{j=1}^{R-1}p_{(j)}\delta_{x_{(j)}}+\tau_{R-1}u,
    \qquad
    v:=\frac{1}{\tau_{R-1}}\sum_{j=R}^{V^L}p_{(j)}\delta_{x_{(j)}}.
\]
Since Dirac measures and the uniform distribution are product distributions, $q_R\in\mathcal M_{1,R}$.
Furthermore, $p^\star=\sum_{j=1}^{R-1}p_{(j)}\delta_{x_{(j)}}+\tau_{R-1}v$. 
By the convexity of KL divergence,
\begin{align*}
    \mathsf{Proj}_{1,R}(p^\star)
    &\leq D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p^\star\|q_R)
     \leq\tau_{R-1}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(v\|u)\\
    &=\tau_{R-1}\big(L\log V-H(v)\big)
     \leq\tau_{R-1}L\log V.
\end{align*}
To bound the remaining mass $\tau_{R-1}$, notice that
\[
    \tau_{R-1}
    =\sum_{j\geq R}p_{(j)}^\alpha p_{(j)}^{1-\alpha}
    \leq p_{(R)}^{1-\alpha}S_\alpha,
    \quad \text{and }
    R\, p_{(R)}^\alpha\leq\sum_{j=1}^R p_{(j)}^\alpha\leq S_\alpha.
\]
Therefore,
\[
    \tau_{R-1}\leq
    \bigg(\frac{S_\alpha}{R}\bigg)^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}S_\alpha
    =\bigg(\frac{e^{H_\alpha(p^\star)}}{R}\bigg)^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha}.
\]
Combining this bound with $\tau_{R-1}\leq1$ and $\mathcal M_{1,R}\subseteq\mathcal M_{J,R}$ proves \eqref{eq:renyi-error-bound}.

name: Lemma \reflem:renyi-compression

label: ass:class
title: \bf Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:class}
    Let $\mathcal{F}(\Theta)$ be a logit function class on $\overline{\mathbb V}^L$. 
    Suppose that there exist constants $G\ge 0$ and $C(\Theta)\ge 1$ such that 
                                            
    \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
        \item Boundedness. For every $\theta \in \Theta$ and any position $i\in [L]$, token $v\in \mathbb V$, it holds that 
        $-G\le F_{\theta,i,v}(x)\le0$ for any $F_{\theta} \in \mathcal{F}(\Theta)$ and any input $x\in \overline{\mathbb V}^L$. 
                                                                                               
        \item Capacity. For any $\eta\in (0,1]$, the covering number satisfies  
        \[
        \log\mathcal N(\eta,\mathcal F(\Theta),d_\infty)\le C(\Theta)\log(e/\eta).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Logit class

label: prop:oracle
title: \bf Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:oracle}
    Fix integers $n,V\ge3$, and a masking schedule $s$ in Section~\ref{sec:mdm}. 
                                                                               
    Suppose that $\mathcal{F}(\Theta)$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:class} with parameters $G$ and $C(\Theta)$, 
    and let $\widehat{\theta} \in \arg \min_{\theta \in \Theta} \widehat{R}_n(p_{\theta})$ be an exact ERM estimator over the induced predictor class $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{F}}(\Theta)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Here the population excess risk is defined as $\mathcal{L}(\theta) := \overline{R}(p_{\theta}) - \overline{R}(p^\star)$ for $p_{\theta} \in \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{F}}(\Theta)$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    Let $M_G:=G+\log V$. 
                                                                                                                                                                                           
    Then
                                                                                     
                                                                      
                                               
                                                           
    \begin{equation}
    \mathbb E\big[\mathcal L(\widehat\theta)\big]
    \lesssim  \inf_{\theta \in \Theta} \mathcal{L} (\theta)
        +M_G \cdot \frac{C(\Theta)\log(en)+1}{n}.
    \label{eq:prop oracle}
    \end{equation}
    Here the expectation is taken over training data $\{X^{(j)}\}_{j=1}^n$.

label: lem:cover
title: \bf Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cover}
Let $\Theta=\Theta(D,N,M,D_{\mathrm{ff}},B,S;R_{\mathrm{embed}},G)$ be the parameter class in Section \ref{sec:estimator}, with $D,N,M,D_{\mathrm{ff}}\geq1$ and $B,R_{\mathrm{embed}},G>0$. Define
\[
    P_{\mathrm{tr}}
    :=(V+1)D+LD+N(3MD^2+2DD_{\mathrm{ff}})+DV = O(DV+LD+NMD^2+NDD_{\mathrm{ff}}),
\]
and suppose the sparsity $1\leq S\leq P_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is an integer. 
There exists a constant $A_{\mathrm{TF}}\geq e$, depending only on $N$, $M$, $B$, $R_{\mathrm{embed}}$, satisfying
\[
    \log A_{\mathrm{TF}}
    \leq CN^2\log\big(eNM(B\vee1)(R_{\mathrm{embed}}\vee1)\big),
\]
such that, for every $0<\eta\leq1$,
\begin{align}
    \log\mathcal N(\eta,\mathcal F(\Theta),d_\infty)
    \leq S\log\frac{eP_{\mathrm{tr}}}{S}
        +S\log\frac{A_{\mathrm{TF}}}{\eta}.
    \label{eq:sparse-cover}
\end{align}
Consequently, Assumption~\ref{ass:class} holds with
\[
    C(\Theta)
    =S\bigg[\log\frac{eP_{\mathrm{tr}}}{S}
            +\log A_{\mathrm{TF}}\bigg].
\]
The same covering bound holds for the probability-valued predictor class in the uniform distance: 
$$\max_{x\in \overline{\mathbb V}^L} \max_{i,v} |p_{\theta,i}(v|x)-p_{\theta',i}(v|x)|.$$
If $S>P_{\mathrm{tr}}$, replace $S$ by $P_{\mathrm{tr}}$ in these bounds.
head: environment
name: Capacity of the sparse transformer class

title: Proof
body_md:
We first control the change in the logits under a perturbation of the parameters, and then cover the sparse parameter space. Write $\|Z\|_{2,\infty}:=\max_i\|Z_{i,\cdot}\|_2$, and let $d_\Theta(\theta,\theta')$ be the largest Frobenius distance between corresponding parameter matrices, including $E,P$, and $W_{\mathrm{out}}$. Set
\[
    \overline B:=B\vee1,\qquad
    \overline R:=R_{\mathrm{embed}}\vee1,\qquad
    a:=eNM\overline B\,\overline R.
\]

For $\|Z\|_{2,\infty}\leq r$, the bounded attention activation gives
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathrm{head}_\theta(Z)_{i,\cdot}\|_2
    &\leq\frac1L\sum_{j=1}^L
      \big|\sigma_{\mathrm{attn}}
        (\langle Z_{i,\cdot}Q,Z_{j,\cdot}K\rangle)\big|
      \|Z_{j,\cdot}V\|_2
    \leq Br.
\end{align*}
Hence the attention layer maps the row radius $r$ to at most $(1+MB)r$. The feed-forward layer multiplies this radius by at most $1+B^2$, since ReLU is one-Lipschitz and vanishes at zero. Denoting the hidden states by $H_\theta^{(\ell)}(x)$, with $H_\theta^{(0)}(x)=\mathsf{Embed}_{E,P}(x)$, we obtain
\[
    \|H_\theta^{(\ell)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
    \leq R_{\mathrm{embed}}\big[(1+MB)(1+B^2)\big]^\ell
    \leq a^{cN},\qquad 0\leq\ell\leq N,
\]
uniformly over $x$ and $\theta\in\Theta$.

Next, let $\Delta:=d_\Theta(\theta,\theta')$. The trainable embeddings satisfy
\[
    \|H_\theta^{(0)}(x)-H_{\theta'}^{(0)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
    \leq\|E-E'\|_{\mathrm F}+\|P-P'\|_{\mathrm F}
    \leq2\Delta.
\]
For one attention head, the sigmoid activation is $1/4$-Lipschitz. For inputs $Z,Z'$ with row norms at most $r$, we have
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathrm{head}_\theta(Z)
      -\mathrm{head}_\theta(Z')\|_{2,\infty}
    &\leq\big(B+\tfrac12 B^3r^2\big)
           \|Z-Z'\|_{2,\infty},\\
    \|\mathrm{head}_\theta(Z)
      -\mathrm{head}_{\theta'}(Z)\|_{2,\infty}
    &\leq\big(r+\tfrac12 B^2r^3\big)\Delta.
\end{align*}
For the feed-forward layer, the corresponding bounds are
\begin{align*}
    \|\mathsf{FFN}_\theta(Z)
      -\mathsf{FFN}_\theta(Z')\|_{2,\infty}
    &\leq(1+B^2)\|Z-Z'\|_{2,\infty},\\
    \|\mathsf{FFN}_\theta(Z)
      -\mathsf{FFN}_{\theta'}(Z)\|_{2,\infty}
    &\leq2Br\Delta.
\end{align*}
Combining these bounds with the hidden-state bound gives
\[
    \|H_\theta^{(\ell)}(x)-H_{\theta'}^{(\ell)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
    \leq a^{cN}\big(
       \|H_\theta^{(\ell-1)}(x)-H_{\theta'}^{(\ell-1)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
       +\Delta\big).
\]
Starting from the embedding perturbation bound and iterating over $N$ blocks, we obtain
\[
    \|H_\theta^{(N)}(x)-H_{\theta'}^{(N)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
    \leq a^{cN^2}\Delta,
\]
after increasing the universal constant $c$.

For the output embedding, let $\|\cdot\|_{\infty,\infty}$ denote the largest absolute matrix entry. Then
\begin{align*}
    &\|H_\theta^{(N)}(x)W_{\mathrm{out}}
       -H_{\theta'}^{(N)}(x)W'_{\mathrm{out}}\|_{\infty,\infty}\\
    &\qquad\leq
       B\|H_\theta^{(N)}(x)-H_{\theta'}^{(N)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
       +\|H_{\theta'}^{(N)}(x)\|_{2,\infty}
        \|W_{\mathrm{out}}-W'_{\mathrm{out}}\|_{\mathrm F}\\
    &\qquad\leq a^{cN^2}\Delta.
\end{align*}
Since clipping is one-Lipschitz, taking the supremum over masked sequences yields
\[
    d_\infty(F_\theta,F_{\theta'})
    \leq\Lambda d_\Theta(\theta,\theta'),
    \qquad \Lambda:=a^{cN^2}.
\]

It remains to cover the parameters. The input and positional embeddings have $(V+1)D+LD$ entries, each transformer block has $3MD^2+2DD_{\mathrm{ff}}$ entries, and the output embedding has $DV$ entries. This gives the stated value of $P_{\mathrm{tr}}$.

For a fixed support $\mathcal I\subseteq[P_{\mathrm{tr}}]$ of size $S$, denote
\[
    \Theta_{\mathcal I}
    :=\{\theta\in\Theta:\mathsf{supp}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal I\}.
\]
Ignoring the embedded-input constraint temporarily, the parameters on this support lie in a product of Frobenius balls of radius $B$, with total dimension $S$. Covering each ball at radius $\zeta/2$ gives a product cover of size at most $(1+4B/\zeta)^S$ in the maximum Frobenius distance. For each ball intersecting $\Theta_{\mathcal I}$, choose one parameter from the intersection as its new center. The radius is then at most $\zeta$, and every center satisfies all constraints, including the embedded-input bound. Consequently,
\[
    \log\mathcal N(\zeta,\Theta_{\mathcal I},d_\Theta)
    \leq S\log\bigg(1+\frac{4B}{\zeta}\bigg).
\]
Every parameter with at most $S$ nonzero entries belongs to one of these support classes. Taking the union over supports gives
\begin{align*}
    \log\mathcal N(\zeta,\Theta,d_\Theta)
    &\leq\log\binom{P_{\mathrm{tr}}}{S}
       +S\log\bigg(1+\frac{4B}{\zeta}\bigg)\\
    &\leq S\log\frac{eP_{\mathrm{tr}}}{S}
       +S\log\bigg(1+\frac{4B}{\zeta}\bigg).
\end{align*}
Take $\zeta=\eta/\Lambda$ and $A_{\mathrm{TF}}:=e(1+4B\Lambda)$. Transferring the parameter cover to the logits proves \eqref{eq:sparse-cover}, and
\[
    \log A_{\mathrm{TF}}
    \leq CN^2\log\big(eNM(B\vee1)(R_{\mathrm{embed}}\vee1)\big).
\]
Since $A_{\mathrm{TF}}\geq e$ and $0<\eta\leq1$, the covering bound is at most $C(\Theta)\log(e/\eta)$. The logits already lie in $[-G,0]$, so both parts of Assumption~\ref{ass:class} hold.

Finally, softmax is one-Lipschitz in the maximum norm. Applying it rowwise therefore transfers the same cover to the predictor class. This completes the proof.
head: manual
name: Lemma \reflem:cover

label: lem:localized-entropy
title: \bf Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:localized-entropy}
Let $X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}$ be independent samples from a distribution $P$, and write $Pg:= \mathbb E[g(X)]$ and $P_n g:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n g(X^{(i)})$ for any function $g$.
Let $\mathcal G$ be a nonempty function class with $\|g\|_\infty\le b$ and $Pg^2\le\sigma^2$ for every $g\in\mathcal G$, where $b\ge1$. Suppose $v\ge1$, $A\ge e$, and 
\[
 \log\mathcal N(\eta,\mathcal G,\|\cdot\|_\infty)
 \le v\log(A/\eta),\quad \forall \, 0<\eta\le1.
\]
For $n\ge2$, take $d_n:=v\log(cAn)$, for a universal $c\ge2$. Then 
                                       
    
                            
                                                
                                                     
                                                            
    
                                                                     
for $t>0$, with probability at least $1-e^{-t}$,
\[
 \sup_{g\in\mathcal G}(P-P_n)g
 \le C\Big(\sigma\sqrt{\frac{d_n+t}{n}}+\frac{b(d_n+t)}n\Big).
\]
head: environment
name: Localized bounds from a uniform cover

title: Proof
body_md:
Take an internal $1/n$-net $\{g_1,\ldots,g_{J_{\rm net}}\}\subseteq\mathcal G$. 
If covering centers are initially outside the class, start with a $1/(2n)$-cover and choose one element of each intersecting ball. 
Thus $\log(2J_{\rm net})\le v\log(4An)\le d_n$ after increasing $c$. All centers retain the variance and envelope bounds.

For the deviation assertion, the independent centered variables $Pg_j-g_j(X^{(i)})$ have magnitude at most $2b$ and variance at most $\sigma^2$. Bernstein's inequality and a union bound then give
\[
 \max_{1\le j\le J_{\rm net}}(P-P_n)g_j
 \le \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma^2(\log J_{\rm net}+t)}n}
      +\frac{2b(\log J_{\rm net}+t)}{3n}
\]
with probability at least $1-e^{-t}$. Replacing a function by its net center changes $(P-P_n)g$ by at most $2/n$, which is absorbed in $b(d_n+t)/n$.

label: lem:regularization
title: \bf Lemma
head: environment
name: Properties of $\delta$-regularization

label: eq:proof-refresh-factorization
title: Proof
body_md:
For part (i), fix a representation $q=\sum_{r=1}^R\pi_rq_r$ as in Section~\ref{sec:problem setup}. Notice that
\[
    \sum_{a\in\mathbb V}B_{i,r}(a,z)Q_\delta(a,v)
    =(1-\delta)B_{i,r}(v,z)+\frac\delta V
    =B_{i,r}^\delta(v,z).
\]
Substituting the hidden-tree factorization into \eqref{eq:refresh} gives
\begin{align}
    (P_\delta q_r)(y)
    &=\sum_{z\in[J]^L}\nu_r(z_{o_r})
      \prod_{i\ne o_r}A_{i,r}(z_i,z_{\operatorname{pa}_r(i)})
      \prod_{i=1}^L\bigg[\sum_{a\in\mathbb V}
          B_{i,r}(a,z_i)Q_\delta(a,y_i)\bigg]\notag\\
    &=\sum_{z\in[J]^L}\nu_r(z_{o_r})
      \prod_{i\ne o_r}A_{i,r}(z_i,z_{\operatorname{pa}_r(i)})
      \prod_{i=1}^L B_{i,r}^\delta(y_i,z_i)
      =q_r^\delta(y).
    \label{eq:proof-refresh-factorization}
\end{align}
Thus, regularization changes only the emission tables. By linearity, $q^\delta=\sum_{r=1}^R\pi_rq_r^\delta\in\mathcal M_{J,R}$. Since \eqref{eq:refresh} is defined using the observed law $q$, the resulting law does not depend on the chosen hidden-tree representation.

For part (ii), the bounds $Q_\delta(a,b)\geq\rho_\delta$ and $Q_\delta(a,a)\geq1-\delta$ imply
\begin{align}
    q^\delta(y)
    &\geq\sum_{x\in\mathbb V^L}q(x)\rho_\delta^L
     =\rho_\delta^L,
    \label{eq:proof-refresh-full-support}\\
    q^\delta(y)
    &\geq q(y)\prod_{i=1}^LQ_\delta(y_i,y_i)
     \geq(1-\delta)^Lq(y).
    \label{eq:proof-refresh-domination}
\end{align}
Fix a masked sequence $c$ and write $W=W(c)$. Summing over the coordinates outside $W$ gives
\[
    \mathbb P_{X\sim q^\delta}[X_W=c_W]
    =\sum_{x\in\mathbb V^L}q(x)\prod_{j\in W}Q_\delta(x_j,c_j)
    \geq\rho_\delta^{|W|}>0.
\]
Hence, for $i\notin W$ and $v\in\mathbb V$,
\[
    q_i^\delta(v\mid c)
    =\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathbb V^L}q(x)
        Q_\delta(x_i,v)\prod_{j\in W}Q_\delta(x_j,c_j)}
       {\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathbb V^L}q(x)
        \prod_{j\in W}Q_\delta(x_j,c_j)}
    \geq\rho_\delta.
\]
                                                                            

For part (iii), the result is immediate if $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)=+\infty$. Otherwise, applying \eqref{eq:proof-refresh-domination} yields
\begin{align*}
    D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q^\delta)-D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)
    &=\sum_{y:p(y)>0}p(y)\log\frac{q(y)}{q^\delta(y)}\\
    &\leq L\log\frac1{1-\delta}.
\end{align*}
This proves the lemma. 
In particular, regularization also preserves any restriction on the component tree topologies, including a prescribed height bound.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fixing $z_i=z$ in the subtree factorization gives
\[
 \alpha_i(z,c)
 =\sum_{(z_u)_{u\in\mathcal V_i\setminus\{i\}}}
      \prod_{u\in\mathcal V_i\setminus\{i\}}A_u(z_u,z_{\operatorname{pa}(u)})
      \prod_{u\in\mathcal V_i}g_u(z_u,c).
\]
Each summed state ranges over $[J]$. Grouping the sum by child subtrees gives \eqref{eq:message-identities-upward}, starting with $\alpha_i=g_i$ at leaves. Thus $\alpha_i(z,c)$ is the likelihood of the subtree evidence with its root state fixed to $z$. This finite-sum definition also applies to states with $\mathbb P_q[Z_i=z]=0$.

We next verify that $\beta_i(z,c)=\mathbb P_q[Z_i=z,c_{\mathcal V_i^c}]$. It holds at the root since $\mathcal V_o^c=\varnothing$. For $i\ne o$, let $j=\operatorname{pa}(i)$. The evidence outside $\mathcal V_i$ consists of the evidence outside $\mathcal V_j$, the observation at $j$ if present, and the evidence in the sibling subtrees. The tree factorization therefore gives
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb P_q[Z_i=z,c_{\mathcal V_i^c}]
 &=\sum_{a=1}^J A_i(z,a)\mathbb P_q[Z_j=a,c_{\mathcal V_i^c}]\\
 &=\sum_{a=1}^J A_i(z,a)\beta_j(a,c)g_j(a,c)
            \prod_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(j)\setminus\{i\}}m_u(a,c)
 =\beta_i(z,c).
\end{align*}
Factoring the evidence into $\mathcal V_i$ and its complement proves \eqref{eq:message-identities-joint}. At a masked position, the emission at $i$ is absent from the context, so
\[
 \mathbb P_q[X_i=v,c]=\sum_{z=1}^J B_i(v,z)\mathbb P_q[Z_i=z,c].
\]
Dividing by $q(c)>0$ gives \eqref{eq:message-identities-conditional}. Finally, for the mixture,
\[
 \mathbb P_q[X_i=v,c]=\sum_{r=1}^R\pi_r\mathbb P_{q_r}[X_i=v,c],
 \qquad q(c)=\sum_{r=1}^R\pi_rq_r(c).
\]
Apply the single-tree joint identities to each component and take the ratio to obtain \eqref{eq:message-identities-mixture}. This argument does not require every component to assign positive probability to the context.

title: Proof
body_md:

As in Appendix~\ref{app:single-tree-parallel}, all relevant log probabilities lie in $[-LH,0]$. Below, the tables and messages refer to $q^\gamma$, and the superscript $\gamma$ on the hidden tables is suppressed.

Use the embedding and exact table initialization from Appendix~\ref{app:single-tree-parallel} to store $\log A_i$, $\log B_i$, $\log g_i$, and $\log\nu$ at the root. Allocate separate coordinates for the upward and downward log messages, received values, candidates, and LSE workspace. Initialize $\widehat\beta_o^{\log}=\log\nu$, with other message and temporary coordinates zero. Here the superscript $\log$ indicates a stored approximation to a log message. Set
\[
 \eta:=\frac{\varepsilon}{128L(h+1)},\qquad
 t:=\log(eJ/\eta),\qquad \lambda:=\log(L^2H/\eta).
\]
The attention maps in \eqref{eq:single-tree-routing} have error at most $\eta$ per received coordinate. We use the exact clipping, selection, and reset operations from Appendix~\ref{app:single-tree-parallel}, and LSE networks of accuracy $\eta$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:nn-lse-approx}.

label: prop:appendix-message-mixture
title: \bf Proposition
head: environment
name: Height-dependent approximation of regularized mixture logits

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a representation $q=\sum_{r=1}^R\pi_rq_r\in\mathcal M_{J,R}^h$ with component heights at most $h$. Regularize the emissions as in Lemma~\ref{lem:regularization} and apply Lemma~\ref{lem:single-tree-message} to each $q_r^\delta$ with accuracy $a:=\varepsilon/64$. The resulting internal coordinates satisfy
\[
 |\widehat f_{i,r,v}(c)-\log q_{r,i}^\delta(v\mid c)|\le a,
 \qquad |\widehat h_{i,r}(c)-\log q_r^\delta(c)|\le a,
\]
where the first bound is for masked positions and the second holds for every context. These estimates already include the hidden-table perturbation. The branches occupy disjoint auxiliary coordinates and share the input embedding. Run the upward stages for all components, followed by their downward stages, with inactive stages padded by identities.

Use the weights $\pi_r^\kappa$ and the final $V+1$ LSE networks from Appendix~\ref{app:tree-parallel-mixture}. That calculation uses only the two displayed approximation bounds. The two LSE errors are at most $2a$ and $3a$, and the weight perturbation contributes at most $\varepsilon/32$ by \eqref{eq:parallel-mixture-weight-error}. Thus,
\[
 \sup_{c:\,W(c)\ne[L]}\max_{i\notin W(c),\,v\in\mathbb V}
 |F_{\theta,i,v}(c)-F_{i,v}^{\delta,q}(c)|
 \le5a+\varepsilon/32<\varepsilon.
\]

It remains to count the architecture. Take $t=C\log(eLRJ/\varepsilon)$ with a sufficiently large universal constant. Each message stage has depth $Ct^2$, total arithmetic width $CRJ^2t^3$, and arithmetic sparsity $CRJ^2t^8$. The positional routing count in Lemma~\ref{lem:single-tree-message} gives $O(RL)$ nonzeros over each complete pass. Initialization costs $O(LR(J^2+JV))$, the component output groups cost $O(RJVt^8)$, and the final mixture LSEs cost $O(RVt^8)$. Therefore,
\begin{align*}
 N&\le C(h+1)t^2,\\
 S&\le CR\big\{L(J^2+JV)+(h+1)J^2t^8+JVt^8\big\}
   \le CRL(J^2+JV)t^8.
\end{align*}
Widths and sparsities add across components, while their depths are maximized. All workspace is reused across stages. Since $t\le Cb_R$, the width and Frobenius estimates from Lemma~\ref{lem:single-tree-message} give \eqref{eq:height-mixture-budgets}. There is at most one routing head per component at each step. If the rooted topologies coincide, their routing matrices are shared, and the value maps can be combined into one head.

These budgets are uniform over all component trees of height at most $h$. For fixed topologies, the permitted coefficient locations are independent of the tables. Padding to the displayed budgets and allowing the supports to vary gives one class $\Theta$ satisfying \eqref{eq:height-mixture-uniform-realization}. 
This proves the proposition.
Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:decomp} gives the corresponding approximation bound
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}(\Theta)
 \le\frac{s_{\max}}L\mathsf{Proj}_{\mathcal M_{J,R}^h}(p^\star)
     +s_{\max}\log\frac1{1-\delta}+2\varepsilon.
\]
The height bound enters the transformer depth through $h+1$. No logarithmic-height assumption is used.

title: \bf Theorem
head: environment
name: Estimation error for shallow tree

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall $\beta:= \log (enLVJR)$. 
                                                                                                                                                     
Lemma~\ref{lem:decomp} gives
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}(\Theta_h)
 \le\frac{s_{\max}}L\mathsf{Proj}_{\mathcal M_{J,R}^h}(p^\star)
      +\frac{2s_{\max}+2}{n}.
\]
                                                                                                                                                                      
The height-dependent budgets satisfy
\[
 N\le C(h+1)\beta^2,\qquad
 S\le CRL(J^2+JV)\beta^8,\qquad
 \log B\le C\beta^2,\qquad \log P_{\rm tr}\le C\beta.
\]
                                                                
    
                                              
                                               
                                         
    
                                          
Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:gen error} with 
$$ \log A_{\mathrm{TF}} \lesssim h^2\beta^6, \quad C(\Theta_h) \lesssim K_{\rm sh} \beta^{14}$$
yields 
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\big[\mathcal L(\widehat\theta_h)\big]
 \le C\bigg\{\frac{s_{\max}}L\mathsf{Proj}_{J,R}^h(p^\star)
       +\frac{K_{\mathrm{sh}}\beta^{16}}{n}\bigg\} . \label{eq:score estimation of bounded height}
\end{align}
This proves Theorem \ref{thm:shallow-tree-mixture-estimation}.

label: thm:shallow end-to-end
title: \bf Theorem
head: environment
name: Sampling guarantees under shallow tree structure

title: Proof
body_md:
For $1\le h\le L-1$, use the parameter class $\Theta_h$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-message-mixture} with $\delta = \varepsilon = 1/n$. 
Denote $\widehat{\theta}_h $ as the ERM estimator over $\Theta_h$, and let $p_{Y\mid S}$ be the output distribution of the sampler using $p_{\widehat{\theta}_h}$ as mask predictor and $S=(S^1,\ldots,S^T)$ as the unmasking partition.
Then applying the decomposition \eqref{eq:sampling-decomposition} with $\theta = \widehat{\theta}_h$, 
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb E_{\{X^{(j)}\}, S}\big[
        D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p^\star\|p_{Y\mid S})
    \big]
    &=\varepsilon_{\mathsf{parall}}(p^\star; s)
      +L\mathbb E_{ \{X^{(j)}\}}\big[\mathcal L(\widehat\theta_h)\big]\\
    &\lesssim \varepsilon_{\mathsf{parall}}(p^\star; s) + s_{\max}\mathsf{Proj}_{J,R}^h(p^\star) + \frac{LK_{\rm sh}}{n} \mathsf{poly}\log(n,L,V,J,R). 
\end{align*}
Here we apply \eqref{eq:score estimation of bounded height} and $K_{\rm sh}:= RL (J^2+JV)h^2$.

label: lem:nn-clipping
title: \bf Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nn-clipping}
For $a\le b$, define
\[
 \operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(x):=\min\{b,\max\{a,x\}\}.
\]
This function is represented exactly by a ReLU network in
$\mathsf{NN}(2,2,B_{\rm clip},7)$, where
$B_{\rm clip}:=\max\{1,|a|,|b|\}$.
Moreover, for all $x,x'\in\mathbb R$ and $y\in[a,b]$,
\[
 |\operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(x)-\operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(x')|
 \le |x-x'|,
 \quad
 |\operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(x)-y|\le |x-y|.
\]
head: environment
name: Exact realization of clipping

title: Proof
body_md:
The identity
\[
 \operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(x)
 =a+\operatorname{ReLU}(x-a)-\operatorname{ReLU}(x-b)
\]
gives an exact representation with two hidden units, two affine layers,
and at most seven nonzero weights and biases, each of magnitude at most
$B_{\rm clip}$. The clipping function is continuous and piecewise affine
with slopes in $\{0,1\}$, hence is $1$-Lipschitz.
Since $\operatorname{Clip}_{[a,b]}(y)=y$ for $y\in[a,b]$,
the second inequality follows from the first.

\begin{lemma}[Implementation of ReLU DNNs by transformer FFN blocks]
\label{lem:nn-compilation}
Suppose a feed-forward ReLU network has maximum layer dimension $W$, depth $d$, coefficient bound $B\ge1$, and sparsity $S$. 
Using a preserved constant coordinate and two reusable buffers, the function can be implemented rowwise by $O(d+1)$ residual FFN blocks as defined in \eqref{eq:single transformer block} with zero attention updates, auxiliary dimension $O(W)$, FFN width $O(W)$, matrix Frobenius norms at most $C(W+1)(B+1)$, and total sparsity
\[
 C\big(S+(d+1)W\big).
\]
For parallel realization, the sparsities and buffer dimensions add; the squared Frobenius norms add across the branches.
\end{lemma}

head: environment
name: Implementation of ReLU DNNs by transformer FFN blocks

title: Proof
body_md:
Write the ReLU network as
\[
z_0=x,\quad
z_\ell=\operatorname{ReLU}(A_\ell z_{\ell-1}+b_\ell)
\quad (1\le\ell<d), \quad z_d = A_d z_{d-1}+b_d. 
\]
and pad all layer vectors to dimension $W$.
Set all attention updates to zero, and reserve two groups
of $W$ auxiliary coordinates together with a constant coordinate.

Suppose the current row is $h=(z^\top,v^\top,1)$, where
$z$ contains the current NN input and $v$ contains the old
values in the destination coordinates. To implement
$z\mapsto\operatorname{ReLU}(Az+b)$, choose
\[
W_{\rm TF}=
\begin{pmatrix}
A^\top&0&0\\
0&I_W&-I_W\\
b^\top&0&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
U_{\rm TF}=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&I_W&0\\
0&-I_W&0\\
0&I_W&0
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the residual FFN satisfies
\begin{align*}
h+\operatorname{ReLU}(hW_{\rm TF})U_{\rm TF}
&=\big(z^\top,\,
[v+\operatorname{ReLU}(Az+b)-\operatorname{ReLU}(v)+\operatorname{ReLU}(-v)]^\top,\,1\big)\\
&=\big(z^\top,\operatorname{ReLU}(Az+b)^\top,1\big).
\end{align*}
Thus one block writes the next hidden layer exactly.
Alternating the source and destination groups implements
successive layers:
\[
(z_0,0)\longmapsto(z_0,z_1)
\longmapsto(z_2,z_1)\longmapsto(z_2,z_3)
\longmapsto\cdots.
\]

For the final affine layer, take $r=Az+b$ and use four
groups of hidden activations to produce
\[
\Delta v
=\operatorname{ReLU}(r)-\operatorname{ReLU}(-r)-\operatorname{ReLU}(v)+\operatorname{ReLU}(-v)
=r-v.
\]
The residual update therefore gives $v+\Delta v=Az+b$.

To count parameters, let
$s_\ell=\|A_\ell\|_0+\|b_\ell\|_0$.
For each hidden layer, the displayed matrices have
\[
\|W_{\rm{TF},\ell}\|_0=s_\ell+2W,\quad
\|U_{\rm{TF},\ell}\|_0=3W,
\]
while the final affine layer uses at most $2s_d+6W$
nonzero coefficients. Including the initial input copy
and final coordinate selection yields
\[
S_{\rm TF}\le C\big(S+(d+1)W\big).
\]
The construction uses $O(d+1)$ blocks, auxiliary
dimension $O(W)$, and FFN width at most $4W$.
Moreover, for each hidden-layer block,
\[
\|W_{\rm{TF},\ell}\|_F^2
=\|A_\ell\|_F^2+\|b_\ell\|_2^2+2W
\le (W^2+W)B^2+2W,
\quad
\|U_{\rm{TF},\ell}\|_F^2=3W.
\]
The final block satisfies the same bounds up to constants,
so every FFN matrix has Frobenius norm at most
$C(W+1)(B+1)$.
For parallel networks, use disjoint auxiliary and FFN
coordinates; sparsities, auxiliary dimensions, and
squared Frobenius norms then add across branches.

name: Lemma \reflem:nn-compilation

label: lem:nn-softmax-stability
title: \bf Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:nn-softmax-stability}
For any $a,b\in\mathbb R^k$,
\[
 \|\mathrm{softmax}(a)-\mathrm{softmax}(b)\|_1\le2\|a-b\|_\infty.
\]
head: environment
name: Global softmax stability

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $h=a-b$, $z(t)=b+th$, and $p(t)=\mathrm{softmax}(z(t))$ for $0\le t\le1$. Differentiating with respect to $t$ gives
\[
 p'_i(t)=p_i(t)\Big(h_i-\sum_s p_s(t)h_s\Big), \quad \forall i \in [k].
\]
Observe that $p_i(t) \in (0,1]$ together with $\sum_i p_i(t)=1$, and thus
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^k|p'_i(t)| \leq  2\|h\|_{\infty}.
\]
Integrating over $t\in[0,1]$ then proves the result.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform log-sum-exp approximation]\label{lem:nn-lse-approx}
For $n\ge1$ and $0<\xi\le1/2$, there exists a ReLU DNN $\Phi_\xi \in \mathsf{NN}(W,d,B,S)$ such that
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|\Phi_\xi(x)-\operatorname{LSE}(x)|\le\xi,
 \quad \text{where }\operatorname{LSE}(x):=\log\sum_{j=1}^n e^{x_j}.
\]
With $t=\log(en/\xi)$ and some universal constant $C>0$, its network parameters can be chosen as follows,
\[
 d\le Ct^2,\quad W\le Cnt^3,\quad
 S\le Cnt^8,\quad \log B \le Ct^2.
\]
It can be implemented by residual rowwise FFNs with the same orders of depth, width, and sparsity, using reusable auxiliary coordinates and a constant input coordinate. The corresponding matrix Frobenius norms also have logarithms at most $Ct^2$. Moreover, $\operatorname{LSE}$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the infinity norm:
\begin{align}
    |\operatorname{LSE}(x)-\operatorname{LSE}(y)|\le\|x-y\|_\infty. \label{eq:nn-lse-con}
\end{align}
\end{lemma}

head: environment
name: Uniform log-sum-exp approximation

title: Proof
body_md:
For $n=1$, we just take $\Phi_\xi(x)=x_1$. In the following, assume that $n\ge2$ and denote
\[
 \nu:=\frac{\xi}{4n},\quad \eta:=\frac{\xi}{2},
 \quad \text{and }t:=\log(\frac{en}{\xi}).
\]
We construct the approximation by composing the exponential and logarithm networks in Lemmas~\ref{lem:nn-exponential} and~\ref{lem:nn-logarithm} respectively, together with exact maximum, affine, and clipping operations.

name: Lemma \reflem:nn-lse-approx

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $r:=\|x-y\|_\infty$. Then
\[
 y_j-r\le x_j\le y_j+r\quad\text{for every }j
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 e^{-r}\sum_{j=1}^n e^{y_j}
 \le\sum_{j=1}^n e^{x_j}
 \le e^r\sum_{j=1}^n e^{y_j}.
\]
Taking logarithms yields
$\operatorname{LSE}(y)-r\le\operatorname{LSE}(x)\le\operatorname{LSE}(y)+r$, and thus proves the 1-Lipschitz continuity.
